item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 2, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
People’s Daily: This year marks the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. Yesterday, President Xi Jinping attended in Bishkek the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO and the SCO Plus Meeting. Could you please provide more information on this? Guo Jiakun: On September 1, President Xi Jinping attended the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and delivered important remarks titled “Toward Higher Quality Development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.” President Xi pointed out that over the past 25 years, the SCO has traveled an extraordinary journey. Its biggest achievement is that it has steadily grown into a new type of regional cooperation organization with the largest land area and population and enormous development potential. Its most valuable spiritual asset is that it pioneered, and has since followed invariably, the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development. Its most important experience for cooperation is that it has found the right way of coexistence featuring non-alliance, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, enabling regional countries to build a common home together. President Xi put forward four points for the SCO’s future development, namely, staying committed to putting development first and opening up the prospects for shared prosperity, staying committed to taking security as a key goal and fostering an environment of common security, staying committed to a people-centered approach and cementing the foundation for everlasting friendship, and staying committed to dialogue and consultation and striving for more equitable and orderly governance. President Xi stressed that China will work with all parties to continue to hold high the banner of the Shanghai Spirit, implement the development strategy of the SCO for the next decade, and pursue development with higher quality, so as to make greater contributions to a community with a shared future for humanity. On the same day, President Xi attended the SCO Plus Meeting and delivered an important statement titled “Jointly Advocating an Equal and Orderly Multipolar World and Making Global Governance More Just and Equitable.” In his remarks, President Xi provided a profound analysis on questions such as what kind of multipolarity the world needs and how countries and the SCO are going to take part in and promote an equal and orderly multipolar world. He proposed three points on better leveraging the role of the SCO, namely, advancing common prosperity in the vast continent straddling Asia and Europe with the SCO Strength, promoting the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom, and guiding the reform and improvement of global governance through the SCO Action. President Xi stressed that a more united and vibrant SCO is fully capable of making greater contributions to a multipolar world. All parties expressed appreciation for China’s important contribution to the organization’s development as a founding member, and agreed to actively implement the strategic vision set out at the 2025 Tianjin Summit, continue to uphold the Shanghai Spirit, promote institution-building, enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in various areas, strengthen people-to-people bonds, and jointly respond to new types of security challenges, with a view to writing a new chapter of lasting peace and common development. Pheonix TV: We have learned that the Second Meeting of G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors held from August 31 to September 1 failed to issue a communiqué due to China’s differing view on global imbalances. Would you like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: As an important member of the G20, China places high emphasis on the organization’s role as the premier forum for international economic cooperation. Since the United States assumed the 2026 presidency of the G20, the Chinese side has participated in relevant discussions including along the Finance Track in an active and constructive manner and contributed to practical outcomes under various mechanisms. We have noted that parties hold diverging views on certain issues at the recent Meeting of G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors. We regret that the meeting failed to issue a communiqué. The G20, as the premier platform for global economic cooperation, should play its coordinating role on key issues concerning the global economy in an objective, impartial and balanced manner based on the principle of consensus through consultation and equal participation. We hope the United States in its presidency and other members will abide by this principle, give full respect to all parties’ legitimate concerns, and strive for a fruitful Miami Summit. China stands ready to work with the United States to act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and join hands with fellow members to enable the G20 to play a positive role in deepening macroeconomic policy coordination, improving global economic governance, and boosting world economic growth. The Paper: It was reported that the second batch of relief supplies provided by China has been delivered to the Nepalese side yesterday. Can you share more details? Can you also update us on what China has done on sharing information about foreign nationals who remain unaccounted for? Guo Jiakun: The second batch of emergency relief supplies provided by China to Nepal arrived in Kathmandu yesterday afternoon. Five DNA forensic experts were also on the plane to assist Nepal in their operations. The Nepalese side thanked China for urgently sending more supplies and providing technical support. China is preparing the third batch of emergency relief supplies based on the request of Nepal. These supplies will include Bailey bridges, mortuary refrigerators, epidemic prevention supplies and emergency communication equipment. China will also send a second group of DNA experts. In the wake of the disaster, China has kept close communication with relevant countries’ embassies in China to jointly identify missing personnel and properly handle follow-up matters. As we speak, residents of the border areas and pilgrims who were previously stranded in the disaster-hit areas are leaving China via land or air transportation in an orderly manner. Yesterday, the foreign ministry briefed relevant foreign embassies in China on the missing foreign nationals. China will continue to keep the channel of communication with relevant embassies unimpeded by various means. China attaches great importance to the safety of Chinese nationals and institutions in Nepal. We are working with Nepal to make all-out effort to search for and rescue missing Chinese nationals, and assisting the relocation of many Chinese nationals to safety. The Chinese embassy in Nepal will continue to do all we can to assist Chinese nationals in need. AFP: Can the Chinese foreign ministry please provide an updated toll of those who are still missing from the mudslide disaster? Are there new figures since Sunday? And specifically, how many foreigners are missing on the Chinese side? What is the breakdown of their nationalities? How many Chinese citizens are among the dead in Nepal and how many Chinese citizens remain missing in Nepal? Guo Jiakun: The authorities of the Xizang Autonomous Region shared detailed information at the recent press briefing. Yesterday the foreign ministry also informed relevant countries’ embassies in China. According to the latest information, a total of 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries are among those missing. We will continue communicating and coordinating with relevant parties to jointly identify missing persons and properly handle follow-up matters. Nearly 100 Chinese nationals remain unaccounted for in Nepal. We thank the Nepali side for rescuing and transferring Chinese nationals in Nepal and hope these efforts will continue. Ukrinform News Agency: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukraine will intensify deep strikes on military facilities within the Russian territory, which is why the airspace of Russia became dangerous. He has instructed the Ukrainian foreign ministry to inform other countries about the danger of flying in Russian airspace. Chinese airlines companies continue to use Russian skies for passenger and other flights. I’d like to ask whether the foreign ministry has already received a warning from the Ukrainian side and will China respond to the increasing danger？ Guo Jiakun: Dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the Ukraine crisis. We urge the parties concerned to remain calm and exercise restraint, jointly work toward early deescalation and accumulate conditions for the political settlement of the crisis. Asahi Shimbun: Iranian media reported that the Chinese and Iranian leaders had a brief conversation during the SCO Bishkek summit. Can you confirm that? What topics did they discuss? Guo Jiakun: We have released information on President Xi Jinping’s participation in the SCO Bishkek summit, during which he had cordial exchanges with leaders of various countries. Bloomberg: The Russian president and the Chinese leader reportedly discussed holding a trilateral meeting with the U.S. president. That would be when China hosts the APEC summit later this year. Would the foreign ministry like to comment on that? Guo Jiakun: On this question, I have no information to share at the moment. As the host for this year’s APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for the full success of the APEC China Year and make new contribution to the economic growth of the Asia Pacific and beyond. Beijing Daily: Recently, Mr. Ronald Sakolsky returned to China for the first time in 27 years and was reunited with Ms. Yin Yuzhen, a national model worker and renowned figure in China’s fight against desertification. Their moving story has attracted widespread attention. What is your comment? Guo Jiakun: Recently, our American friend Mr. Ronald Sakolsky, affectionately known in China as “Saikaosi” for supporting China’s fight against desertification, visited China upon invitation after 27 years. During his visit, Mr. Sakolsky traveled to Inner Mongolia, where he joined Ms. Yin Yuzhen, a national model worker, and revisited the forest he helped fund years ago, and together planted a tree of friendship. He also returned to the school in Luoyang, Henan Province, where he once taught, to meet with teachers and students. He visited Beijing as well. Throughout his visit, Mr. Sakolsky witnessed firsthand the remarkable changes that have taken place in China and once again experienced the warmth and hospitality of the Chinese people. He was deeply moved and shed tears on several occasions. I noted that in an interview with the media, Mr. Sakolsky said that Ms. Yin and he have shown that they can bridge cultures and break down boundaries. He said that the American and Chinese people both want to live in peace. China and the United States are like two roads, they may take different routes, but they can still lead to the same destination. His sincere words have touched many people. They reflect a shared aspiration of the people of both countries. The hope of the China-U.S. relationship lies in the people, and its foundation lies in grassroots connections. The many inspiring stories written together by the Chinese and American people are a vivid testament to our people-to-people friendship. They also once again demonstrate that China and the United States, as two major countries, can achieve mutual success, and contribute to the well-being of the world. China will, as always, support more visits and exchanges between the two peoples, so that we can continue to write new chapters in our people-to-people friendship and make greater contributions to the development of China-U.S. relations. Global Times: Eighty one years ago today, Japan officially signed the Instrument of Surrender, marking the ultimate triumph of the global fight against fascism. We notice that MFA spokesperson has shared China’s views on the “Enemy State Clauses.” But some believe that there’s no longer an “enemy state” in the world anymore. The “Enemy State Clauses” have expired and are no longer relevant. What’s your take on that? Can you give us more information on China’s position? Guo Jiakun: On September 2, 1945, the Japanese government officially signed the Instrument of Surrender, and accepted all the terms of the Potsdam Proclamation, establishing the undeniable historical conclusion that the war waged by Japan’s militarists was for aggression. It is also a part of the postwar international order that shall not be challenged. The “Enemy State Clauses” are still in the UN Charter and consist of Article 53, 77 and 107. It is a special set of rules for defeated states, aiming to prevent them from threatening international peace and security once again, and has provided important institutional safeguards for defending postwar international order. Japan joined the UN after recognizing its militarist crimes and accepting the UN Charter in its entirety. Today, however, those running the Japanese government keep sidestepping the issue of historical crimes, and even go to great lengths to distort and whitewash its crimes of aggression and move faster to remilitarize Japan. They continue to pay tribute to Class-A war criminals in WWII and attempt to revise the pacifist Constitution. What’s worse, Japan’s ties with nearly all its neighbors have witnessed increased tension. Japan blatantly interferes in the internal affairs of other countries, and even threatens to use force. The “gray rhino” of Japan’s neo-militarism is charging towards us, and posing a threat to peace and stability in the Asia Pacific once again. Against such backdrop, it is extremely necessary to reaffirm the commitment to the UN Charter, in particular, the “Enemy State Clauses.” We urge the Japanese government to earnestly abide by its international obligations stipulated by the Instrument of Surrender, face up to and learn lessons from history, make a clean break with militarism, and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. PTI: Reports say that the high-altitude Himalayan region is warming significantly, faster than the global average. Studies have shown since 1981, the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau have lost roughly 20 percent of its glaciers attributed to the climate change crisis. In the light of the August 26 glacier collapse, how does China view the glacier retreat crisis impacting the Himalayan region and the calls for formation of a coordination mechanism by China with neighbouring countries, to strengthen cooperation to deal with such disasters affecting the fragile region? Guo Jiakun: China has responded to similar questions. According to the assessment of Chinese and Nepali experts, long-term effects of global warming have made glaciers unstable, and this disaster was triggered by the collapse of a glacier in Nepal, resulting in a rapid crash of ice and rocks which took away a chunk of the mountain. The Xizang Autonomous Region shared relevant information at its press conference. China and Nepal have maintained sound cooperation in meteorology, water conservancy and disaster prevention and reduction. In the wake of the disaster, China has shared with Nepal important information such as images, satellite, and hydrological data of the disaster-affected areas, including early-warning information on an upstream barrier lake. We will continue to give strong support to Nepal in its relief efforts and strengthen cooperation on disaster prevention and reduction. Climate change is a common challenge facing all humanity. No country can stay immune from such risks. China will continue to work with the international community to strengthen exchanges and cooperation and effectively prevent and mitigate the negative impact of climate change. As for your specific question, I’d refer you to competent authorities. AFP: I wonder if China has been told if any Chinese citizens were among the dead in Nepal from the disaster last week? And also are you able to provide a specific figure on the number of Chinese nationals missing in China? Guo Jiakun: I just shared the information we have. As we speak, intensive rescue and relief operations are still underway. For the specific information you asked for, there will be continued updates.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 1, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
China News Agency: Could you share with us details about President Xi Jinping’s ongoing state visit to Kyrgyzstan? Guo Jiakun: This is President Xi Jinping’s first state visit to Kyrgyzstan in seven years. During the visit, President Xi Jinping held talks and small group discussions with President Japarov. They had an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in various fields, and international and regional issues of mutual interest. Together, they drew a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. President Xi Jinping noted that China-Kyrgyzstan relations have grown by leaps and bounds in recent years with fruitful cooperation across the board that has contributed to the development of both countries and benefited both peoples. The robust relations have also helped advance regional peace, stability and prosperity. China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to better synergize development strategies, deepen experience sharing on governance and deliver more tangible and on-the-ground results of practical cooperation, so as to expand the depth and substance of the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. President Xi Jinping stressed that the steady and sustained development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations is underpinned by high-level political mutual trust and unwavering mutual support. The signing of the treaty between China and Kyrgyzstan on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will provide an important legal foundation for the two countries to enjoy lasting friendship and unwavering mutual support. China and Kyrgyzstan should deepen bilateral practical cooperation, pursue high-quality cooperation on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a transportation artery carrying the region’s aspirations for development, and carry out more flagship projects in areas such as renewable energy and resource recycling and utilization. The two sides should work together to ensure the success of the Belt and Road Joint Laboratory, step up cooperation in AI and other areas, and further promote personnel exchanges, so as to steadily consolidate public support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship. China and Kyrgyzstan need to expand law enforcement and security cooperation, jointly fight against the three forces of terrorism, separatism and extremism, and combat drugs and transnational crimes, so as to uphold regional peace and stability through concerted efforts. China supports Kyrgyzstan in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs, and will work with Kyrgyzstan to further enhance coordination under the UN framework, jointly implement the four global initiatives, and make the global governance system more just and equitable. Following their talks, the two presidents signed the two countries’ joint declaration on the high-quality development of the comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era and the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation. They witnessed the exchange of bilateral cooperation documents in areas including investment, transport, customs and sister-city relations. During the visit, the two sides signed more than 20 cooperation documents in areas such as science and technology, education, people-to-people exchanges and media. CCTV: Yesterday you shared information about China’s relief assistance to Nepal. Can you update us on China’s plan of further support to Nepal? Guo Jiakun: To provide emergency assistance to Nepal’s disaster-hit areas and carry out international rescue and relief cooperation is an important political decision of China and embodies our friendship with Nepal. The second batch of relief supplies provided by China to Nepal is expected to be sent later today. These supplies include much-needed items such as drones, equipment and reagent for DNA testing, and equipment for water purification and lighting. Chinese DNA testing experts are about to travel to the disaster-hit areas to assist Nepal in their operations. China will stand firmly together with Nepal and jointly overcome the difficulties as part of our efforts to carry forward the traditional friendship as neighboring countries. TASS: Yesterday, during his meeting with President Xi in Bishkek, President Putin said that Russia is ready to make the visa-free regime permanent if the Chinese side considers this possible and useful. What is the foreign ministry’s comment on this? Guo Jiakun: Mutual visa exemption speaks to the high-level strategic mutual trust between China and Russia and helps further facilitate cross-border travel, deepen the friendship between our two peoples, and promote exchanges and cooperation in various fields. Reuters: We reported today that as part of President Trump’s new oil deal with Venezuela, the U.S. oil company, which the U.S. government has a sizable stake in, will take over several oil fields in Venezuela that were previously owned by Chinese companies, including state-owned companies, who have invested in Venezuela for many many years. What is MOFA’s response to this decision? Guo Jiakun: We noted relevant reports. China always advocates that relations between countries should be handled in accordance with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and economic and trade cooperation between countries should follow the principle of equality, mutual benefit and win-win cooperation. Also I would like to stress that China-Venezuela cooperation is protected by international law and laws of both countries. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected. Ukrinform News Agency: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said in an interview that China’s foreign minister assured him that China would not allow Russia to use nuclear weapons in the war in Ukraine. How does the foreign ministry comment on such a statement by the Finnish president? Guo Jiakun: China has released information on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Finland. China’s position on the Ukraine crisis and stance on nuclear-related issues are consistent and clear. We remain committed to promoting peace talks and a political settlement of the crisis. Beijing Daily: Last September, President Xi Jinping solemnly put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI), which received broad and positive responses from the international community. Today marks the first anniversary of President Xi’s proposal of the GGI. Could you please share with us the progress and outcomes achieved by the Initiative over the past year? Guo Jiakun: One year ago today, at the pivotal juncture marking the 80th anniversary of the United Nations, President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Governance Initiative, calling on countries around the world to work together for a more just and equitable global governance system. Over the past year, with its increasing popularity, the Initiative has evolved from a Chinese proposal into international practice, demonstrating strong vitality, influence, and appeal. The GGI has forged broad international consensus. It is fully aligned with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and has quickly won the support and positive responses of nearly 160 countries and international organizations. More than 60 countries have joined the Group of Friends of Global Governance, engaging in intensive coordination on a wide range of global governance issues. BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization have continued to grow, and the representation and voice of the Global South have continued to increase. China is committed to contributing its wisdom to the reform and improvement of global governance. President Xi Jinping delivered important remarks at such events as the Virtual BRICS Summit, the Global Leaders’ Meeting on Women, and the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, providing strategic guidance for global governance to keep pace with the times. China hosted the Lanting Forum on Improving Global Governance to Build a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity, and successively released the Concept Paper on the Global Governance Initiative and a white paper on more just and equitable global governance, further elaborating on China’s visions, principles, and positions on global governance, as well as its action plan. The nine priorities proposed by China for advancing global governance reform have received broad support from the United Nations and the wider international community. We have taken robust actions to translate the GGI into concrete results. The International Organization for Mediation has officially commenced operations and successfully resolved its first international maritime dispute. The World Data Organization and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization have been established in China one after another. At the UN Climate Summit, China announced its 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions. Recently, the official website of the Foreign Ministry launched a dedicated section on the GGI. We welcome everyone to visit the section at any time to follow and support the latest progress in China’s efforts to advance the implementation of the Initiative. The fruitful outcomes achieved by the GGI over the past year have made it abundantly clear that extensive consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits represent the common aspiration of all, that upholding multilateralism is a shared consensus of all, and that building a more just and equitable global governance system is a common expectation of all. China will continue to firmly uphold the UN-centered international system, actively support the robust development of various multilateral and regional cooperation mechanisms, and jointly work for the effective implementation of the GGI. This autumn, we will host the Global Governance Forum in Xiong’an. We look forward to welcoming people from various sectors of the international community to discuss the reform and improvement of global governance and work together for a community with a shared future for humanity. The Sydney Morning Herald: The mudslide is a major catastrophe that has affected many countries’ citizens. Nepal has let in many journalists to cover the situation. Why has China so far refused access to foreign journalists, preventing us from joining Chinese state media reporters on the ground in covering this issue from a disaster zone on the Tibetan side? And secondly, do you have any further information about the Australian who has recently been found alive on the Tibetan side? Guo Jiakun: On your first question, the roads and communication are cut off in the mudslide-affected areas, and there are major safety risks of secondary disasters. Intensive rescue and relief operations are still underway. China will share timely updates about the disaster and rescue and relief operations. On your second question, as I just said, at present, China is making every effort to search for and rescue Chinese and foreign nationals who are still unaccounted for. At the same time, we maintain close communication with foreign embassies in China to jointly identify missing foreign nationals and properly handle follow-up matters. As for the individual case you mentioned, I’ll need to check with competent authorities before getting back to you. Bloomberg: Did Chinese diplomats in the Solomon Islands have any contact with the politicians there who moved a motion of no confidence against Prime Minister Matthew Wale? New Zealand’s foreign minister Winston Peters insinuated that outside forces were involved in that action, which was seen as a reference to China. What’s the foreign ministry’s response on this situation that is developing in the Solomon Islands? Guo Jiakun: On your first question, China adheres to non-interference in other countries’ internal affairs. We have never had any interest in, nor will we ever interfere in any way with the internal affairs of other countries. On your second question, the relevant remarks from the New Zealand side are completely unfounded. China has always adhered to the principle of respecting the sovereignty and independence, will, culture and solidarity of Pacific island countries in developing relations with them. We have no interest in and have never interfered in the internal affairs of other countries. AFP: On President Xi Jinping’s visit to Egypt, can the foreign ministry share any more details about the topics leaders will discuss when they meet for talks? How will China present its position on the Iran war as well as recent promises by the United States to expand sanctions targeting Iran’s economy, which may impact Chinese and Egyptian interests? Guo Jiakun: As we previously stated following the announcement of President Xi Jinping’s upcoming state visit to Egypt, Egypt is the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President El-Sisi, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful outcomes in cooperation across various fields, and engaged in increasingly frequent people-to-people exchanges and close and effective coordination on multilateral occasions. China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has grown by leaps and bounds, and been at its best in history, setting a stellar example of solidarity, coordination, and mutual benefit among developing countries. This visit marks President Xi Jinping’s first state visit to Egypt in 10 years. As we are celebrating the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Egypt diplomatic relations, this visit carries great significance in building on the past achievements and charting the future. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with President El-Sisi. They will have an in-depth exchange of views on China-Egypt relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest. Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other’s modernization, so that we can jointly draw a new chapter of China-Egypt relations and make positive contributions to peace and stability in the region and beyond. Reuters: The U.S. and New Zealand have announced that they are planning to jointly develop a deep sea port on a former military base in the Cook Islands. What is the ministry’s response? Guo Jiakun: Cooperation between countries should be conducive to maintaining regional peace and stability. Reuters: On Nepal, how closely is China keeping Nepal informed of the upstream efforts to drain the lakes formed by last week’s mudslide? Could you give us some details about the communication? Guo Jiakun: China and Nepal have maintained smooth cooperation in fields including meteorology, water conservancy, and disaster prevention and mitigation. In the wake of the disaster, China has maintained sound communication with Nepal on the information sharing for search and rescue and the prevention of secondary disasters, continuously provided meteorological and hydrological information, conducted professional consultations, and sent relevant early warnings. China will continue to strongly support Nepal in disaster relief, strengthen cooperation in disaster prevention and mitigation, and safeguard the common interests of the two peoples. Reuters: About the Power of Siberia II pipeline, are there any discussions that happened in regard to that between the Chinese and Russian leaders? Guo Jiakun: China has released information on the meeting between President Xi and President Putin. China and Russia have cooperated closely in energy and other various fields under the strategic guidance of the two leaders. China stands ready to work with Russia to further deepen practical cooperation under the principle of mutual respect and mutual benefit. ************************************************** ABC: According to Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, an Australian believed to be missing after the mudslide has been found alive. Can you share more details on the time, location and the physical conditions of the person? What channels has China used to share the information with the Australian side? (Similar question from The Sydney Morning Herald during the press conference) Guo Jiakun: We’ve learned that this Australian national was not in the hardest-hit area and has got into contact with the Australian Embassy in Beijing. China is continuing the all-out search and rescue for missing Chinese and foreign nationals. We will stay in close communication with foreign embassies in China to jointly identify missing foreign nationals and properly handle follow-up matters.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on August 31, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
At the invitation of the government of the Russian Federation, from September 2 to 4, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will travel to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum and hold the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum. Xinhua News Agency: With rescue efforts still underway following the mudslide in Gyirong, could you please provide further details on the progress of rescue work related to foreign countries? Guo Jiakun: The devastating mudslide, triggered by a sudden glacial collapse in Nepal’s border area, has caused massive casualties and left many unaccounted for in both China and Nepal. While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. President Xi Jinping sent a condolence message to Nepali President Ram Chandra Poudel. Premier Li Qiang also expressed condolences to the Nepali side. The meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee called for emergency assistance to the affected areas in Nepal and international cooperation in rescue and relief. On August 29, Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke with Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal over the phone. He noted that China and Nepal are a community linked by mountains and rivers and a shared future. In the face of the disaster, the two countries should stand firmly together, join hands to overcome the difficulties, and demonstrate the traditional friendship through concrete actions. The Chinese government has provided Nepal with emergency cash assistance and humanitarian aid. The first batch of 50 tons of relief supplies has already arrived in Kathmandu. Two rescue teams composed of Chinese tunnel rescue experts have rushed to the disaster-stricken areas in Nepal. We have also shared with the Nepali side important information such as images, satellite, and hydrological data of the disaster-affected areas, including early-warning information on an upstream barrier lake. China is actively assisting stranded Nepali citizens in returning to Nepal as soon as possible. As of noon yesterday, all Chinese nationals in Nepal’s disaster-hit areas, with whom contact has been reestablished, have been safely relocated. At present, China is making every effort to search for and rescue Chinese and foreign nationals who are still unaccounted for. At the same time, we maintain close communication with foreign embassies in China to jointly identify missing foreign nationals and properly handle follow-up matters. China News Service: To follow up on your announcement about Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang’s trip to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum and hold the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum, could you share with us the background, program and China’s expectation of the visit? Guo Jiakun: Themed on “The Far East: Development for the Benefit of People,” the 11th Eastern Economic Forum will be held in Vladivostok, Russia from September 1 to 4. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will attend the plenary session of the forum, co-chair the institutionalized meetings of China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee and China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, as well as China-Russia Energy Business Forum with Russian leaders, and hold meetings with them. This year marks the 30th anniversary of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination, and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. China will take this opportunity to implement the important common understandings of the two heads of state, make greater progress in developing the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era, and bring benefits to the two peoples. China also looks forward to working with various parties to step up communication, enhance mutual trust, stick to openness and cooperation, and share the opportunities of development, so as to make greater contribution to promoting regional revitalization and development as well as the common welfare of the people of all countries. CGTN: His Majesty King Harald V of Norway passed away. I wonder if China has any comment? Guo Jiakun: King Harald V was highly esteemed and deeply loved by the Norwegian people. He was committed to promoting China-Norway friendship, paid multiple visits to China and made significant contributions to bilateral exchange and cooperation. China mourns his passing and extends sincere condolences to the royal family, government and people of Norway. Bloomberg: Some Indian TV channels have blamed China for the floods and mudslide disaster. They say China is going ahead with major construction projects in hydropower and infrastructure. Would the ministry like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We noted that experts and official institutions of China and Nepal have made some assessment on the cause of the disaster. According to their analysis, the mudslide was triggered by a collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal. In the face of tragic disasters, we reject malicious speculation that has no factual basis. Sky News: It appears that China has censored and taken down some of the more dramatic videos of that terrible flood smashing into Gyirong Port. Can I ask why China has done that? There have been some suggestions that the numbers of missing and dead are being understated. Can I ask what China’s response is to those accusations? Guo Jiakun: Intensive search, rescue and relief operations are still underway in an orderly manner in the disaster-hit areas. China has been open, transparent and timely in information release. Smear and disinformation is most unwelcome at a time of disaster response. Shenzhen TV: It is reported that the Third APEC Senior Officials’ Meeting concluded in Dalian on August 28. Could you brief us on the meeting and its main outcomes? Guo Jiakun: From August 17 to 28, the Third Senior Officials’ Meeting of APEC China and related meetings were held in Dalian. Deputy Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu attended the meeting and delivered remarks. This was the largest Senior Officials’ Meeting held during the APEC China Year in terms of both attendance and number of events. During the meeting, APEC committees and working groups held nearly 130 meetings and events, covering areas such as trade, transportation, food, customs, science and technology, energy, health, disaster reduction, and anti-corruption. More than 3,000 representatives from APEC member economies, the APEC Secretariat, and APEC observers attended the meetings. Participants held in-depth discussions under the theme of APEC China Year and “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together” and around the three priority areas of “Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation,” and focused on comparing notes on the outcomes for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting to be held in Shenzhen this November. Under the “Openness” priority, China hosted a policy dialogue on connectivity, laying the groundwork for developing an upgraded APEC Connectivity Blueprint. Under the “Innovation” priority, China hosted a policy dialogue on the digital economy and artificial intelligence as drivers of economic growth. Participants held in-depth discussions on leveraging AI to promote economic growth, improve people’s well-being, and bridge the digital divide, continuing the positive momentum generated by APEC Digital Week held in Chengdu in July. Under the “Cooperation” priority, China keeps advancing result‑oriented cooperation covering such areas as anti‑corruption, customs, food security, fisheries and maritime affairs, public health and energy. Major deliverables have been secured on themes such as improving integrity for prosperity and customs cooperation to bolster trade security and facilitation. The final Senior Officials’ Meeting of the APEC China Year will be held in Shenzhen on the eve of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting this November. We welcome reporters to continue following and covering events under the APEC China Year. Reuters: More than 900 people are believed to be stuck inside blocked hydropower project tunnels in Nepal after the flood last week. Were there any Chinese nationals working at these projects and has the government or the ministry identified if any of those Chinese nationals are trapped in the tunnels? Guo Jiakun: Nearly 100 Chinese nationals are among those missing in Nepal. The Nepali side has been trying every possible means to search for and rescue those missing or trapped. Tunnel experts from China have arrived in the affected area in Nepal to assist in rescue efforts. Phoenix TV: Japan’s Self-Defense Forces (SDF) in a statement on August 28 said that they had dismissed SDF officer Kodai Murata. The SDF said it is extremely regrettable that one of its members committed such an act, and it will take thorough measures to have its personnel strictly follow laws and regulations. What is China’s comment? Does this address China’s concerns? Guo Jiakun: It is shockingly malignant for a sitting Japanese SDF officer to break into the Chinese embassy carrying a knife and threaten the Chinese side with violence. This incident seriously violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, gravely threatens the safety and security of Chinese diplomatic personnel and premises, and exposes deep-seated problems in Japan, including the rampant spread of right-wing impact and lack of supervision and discipline in the SDF. We noted that Japanese public prosecutors have indicted the person concerned. We urge the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its duty, bring the perpetrator to account, conduct a thorough investigation and correct the wrongdoings. This is also what the international community hopes to see. Bloomberg: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the world cannot have a US$1.2 trillion trade surplus with China and he said the G20 countries should reexamine their terms of trade with the country. Would the Foreign Ministry like to comment? Guo Jiakun: China‑U.S. economic and trade ties are mutually beneficial in nature. China never seeks trade surplus. We oppose unilateral tariff measures in all forms. Committed to high‑standard opening up, China, with its vast market, offers new opportunities to all, including the United States. Both sides need to act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents, resolve outstanding issues through consultation on the basis of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit, and strive to maintain the hard‑won positive momentum in bilateral trade. ************************************************** Reuters: Nepali officials said that Nepal once asked China to gain access to shared monitoring data on meteorology, rainfall and river conditions in their talks with the Chinese side in May. But there was no formal mechanism agreed. Can you confirm it? Why has no such mechanism been established? What information has China shared with Nepal so far? Has China informed Nepal with unusual signs or early warning indicators before the disaster happened? What measures will China take concerning data sharing with Nepal in the future? Guo Jiakun: China and Nepal maintain sound cooperation in areas of meteorology, water conservation and disaster prevention and control. In the wake of the disaster, China and Nepal have been in smooth communication on search and rescue, information sharing and prevention of secondary disaster. We have been providing Nepal with meteorological and hydrological data, conducted consultation among experts, and shared early-warning information. China will continue giving strong support to Nepal in its relief efforts and strengthen cooperation with Nepal on disaster prevention and control for the shared benefit of both peoples. Reuters: A former Nepali ambassador to the United Nations said that the government’s reluctance to accept foreign search-and-rescue teams may be linked to the sensitivity of the region bordering China’s Xizang. The Nepali foreign ministry has denied this. What is China’s comment？ Guo Jiakun: In the wake of the disaster, the Nepali government has been fully committed to disaster response and relief efforts. The world has reached out to help. The Nepali government’s decisions and requests should be respected, instead of being a target of unwarranted speculation.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 28, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
At the invitation of the government of Zambia, President Xi Jinping’s Special Envoy and Vice Chairperson of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference Xian Hui will attend the inauguration of President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia in Lusaka on September 1. CCTV: We notice that the rescue work in the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County is still ongoing, could you share with us the latest developments? Lin Jian: The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee held a meeting on August 28 to deliberate, plan and deploy work on rescue and relief efforts after a devastating mudslide hit Gyirong County, Xigaze City of Xizang Autonomous Region. General Secretary Xi Jinping chaired the meeting. At the beginning of the meeting, Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the People’s Republic of China and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, proposed that all participants stand for a moment of silence for those who lost their lives in the disaster. It was noted at the meeting that the mudslide in Nepal had caused heavy casualties and left many missing at the Gyirong Port in Gyirong County. In the wake of the mudslide, the CPC Central Committee gave high priority to the disaster response, and General Secretary Xi Jinping immediately made important instructions, setting out clear requirements for rescue operations and emergency response. Entrusted by General Secretary Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Premier of the State Council, travelled to the disaster-hit area to visit those affected and the rescue teams, and provide on-site instruction on rescue and emergency response efforts. Zhang Guoqing, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, also rushed to the site to oversee the operations. Under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee and under the instruction of the State Council working group, the Xizang Autonomous Region, the Ministry of Emergency Management and other relevant departments, as well as professional rescue forces, including firefighting and rescue teams and China Anneng Group, acted swiftly. The People’s Liberation Army and the armed police forces responded immediately to the call and arrived at the affected region in a timely manner. Rescue and relief efforts were carried out in an intensive and orderly manner, while the resettlement of affected people and follow-up work were launched and advanced across the board. It was underlined at the meeting that the disaster happened in a high-altitude, cold region, where valleys are steep and the climate is highly volatile. There are still many glaciers and glacial lakes in the surrounding areas, with considerable geological hazard risks, posing enormous difficulties for rescue and relief efforts. All relevant parties must uphold the principle of putting people and human life first, and ensure that all work is carried out with firm and effective measures and sound and efficient approaches. Sound rescue plans must be formulated, and all-out efforts must be made to search for and rescue missing people from China and abroad. Joint consultations among multiple departments must be strengthened, monitoring and early-warning efforts must be enhanced, close attention must be paid to the stability of the barrier lakes and surrounding mountains, and effective measures must be taken to prevent secondary disasters. On-site personnel management must be strengthened to ensure safety throughout the entire rescue operation. Proper arrangements must be made for affected people, and careful and thorough efforts must be made in providing compensation, relief and other follow-up assistance. We will provide emergency assistance to disaster-hit areas in Nepal, and carry out international rescue cooperation . We will earnestly act on the guiding principles of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, and make all-out efforts for rescue operations, emergency response, and other work related to foreign countries. Reuters: I would like to ask a follow-up question concerning the landslide in Tibet. Are you able to update us today on a breakdown of the nationalities of the casualties? And in particular, are there Indian tourists or pilgrims who have been affected on the Tibetan side? Lin Jian: As I said yesterday, relevant information is under further verification. We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China and will stay in contact with them. China Daily: Results of the Cook Islands parliamentary general election show that the Cook Islands Party led by incumbent Prime Minister Mark Brown won majority seats, securing another term for Mr. Brown. What is China’s comment and expectation for its relations with the Cook Islands? Lin Jian: China congratulates Prime Minister Mark Brown on winning another term. China highly values its relations with the Cook Islands, and stands ready to work with the new government to further deepen political mutual trust, expand practical cooperation in various fields, and strive for greater progress of the comprehensive strategic partnership featuring mutual respect and common development for the benefit of both peoples. The Paper: It is reported that, a civic group in Japan held an exhibition in Yokohama City on Japanese army’s wartime poison gas use. The exhibition aims to expose Japanese military’s wartime production of poison gas and poison gas bombs and its waging of gas warfare against China and Southeast Asian countries during WWII. According to the exhibition, after Japan’s defeat, some chemical weapons were left behind in China, continuing to cause harm to local people. Japanese visitors interviewed at the exhibition said that conducting chemical warfare was an atrocity committed by the Japanese military, and they never learned about this history at school; Japanese forces committed such evil acts, and it is a disgrace for the country. They also said that is why they want to erase it from history; This history must be made clear. We must become people capable of distinguishing right from wrong, they added. What’s your comment? Lin Jian: During WWII, Japanese militarists developed and used chemical weapons on a large scale in China and other Asian countries, which constitutes a blatant violation of international law and has caused untold suffering on multiple countries. In China alone, there are more than 2,000 cases of Japanese forces using chemical weapons, causing more than 200,000 Chinese military and civilian casualties. After Japan’s defeat, in an attempt to cover up its crimes, a large number of chemical weapons were left behind in China, resulting in more than 2,000 casualties so far and posing a serious threat to Chinese people’s lives and the ecological environment. Despite long-existing evidence of the crimes against humanity, Japanese right-wing forces distorted history and falsely claimed that the abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs) have gradually become “not harmful” and that “the legal statutes of limitations for liability have passed.” The Japanese government has demonstrated insufficient sincerity and given inadequate input in fulfilling its obligations of the Chemical Weapons Convention concerning the complete destruction of the ACWs, and the destruction process is seriously lagging behind schedule. To remove the hazardous ACWs is Japanese government’s unshirkable historical responsibility and due obligation under international law. China urges the Japanese government to fulfill its responsibility under relevant convention, face up to the just call from visionary people in its own country and victim neighboring countries, comprehensively and faithfully fulfill the requirements of international convention and the MOU between the two governments, speed up the destruction process, and restore a safe living environment for the Chinese people at an early date. AFP: On the U.S. and Iran, U.S. President Donald Trump yesterday hinted that his administration might be preparing sanctions targeting Chinese institutions over the links to Iran. This is part of U.S. efforts to isolate Iran. What is your response to Donald Trump? Lin Jian: On the Iran situation, we always believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out. China opposes illicit unilateral sanctions. This position is consistent and clear. The Hindu: Two questions on the mudslides. First, has there been any official determination on what actually caused this tragedy? And secondly, there were reports this morning that all 555 stranded tourists had been evacuated. I was just wondering if you had any information on whether there were tourists from India who have been evacuated and also if there are some who are still missing? Lin Jian: We noted that experts and official institutions of China and Nepal have made preliminary assessment on the cause of the disaster. According to their analysis, the disaster has been triggered by a collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal. For more details, please refer to the information released by competent authorities. On your second question, I have made response just now. Relevant information is under further verification. We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China and will stay in contact with them.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 27, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
CCTV: On August 26, a mudslide in Nepal caused heavy casualties and left many missing at Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, Xigaze City of Xizang Autonomous Region. Could you share information on China’s rescue work? Is China in communication with Nepal? Does China have information on the Chinese nationals affected in Nepal and the foreign nationals affected in China? Lin Jian: In the wake of the disaster, General Secretary Xi Jinping attached high importance to the situation and gave immediate instructions. He stressed that the pressing priority is to go all-out in search and rescue, relocate and look after those facing potential danger, provide urgent treatment to the injured, and minimize casualties. It is imperative to step up monitoring and early warning, ensure sound rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for swift verification of the number of missing persons and affected people and all-out rescue and relief efforts to ensure the prompt and orderly evacuation of people in danger. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing has arrived at the site with officials from relevant departments to oversee the rescue and disaster-response operations. Relevant Chinese authorities have activated a national level-II emergency response for disaster relief. Xizang Autonomous Region has activated a level-I emergency response for natural disasters. Rescue forces from the military, armed police, border inspection, firefighting, and other relevant departments have rushed to the affected area at the earliest possible time, to join ongoing search and rescue operations. We are confident that under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee, people in the mudslide-hit area will overcome difficulties and rebuild their homes. The mudslide has caused massive casualties and left many missing in both China and Nepal. The Chinese side extends heartfelt sympathies to the government of Nepal and all those hit by the disaster. The two sides are having close communication and coordinating efforts for the search and rescue. The Chinese side is ready to provide emergency assistance in light of Nepal’s need. According to the information released so far by the local Chinese authorities, a total of 260 foreign nationals remain unaccounted for in the affected areas, with more specifics pending further verification due to the conditions on the ground. For Chinese rescuers, all lives are precious, regardless of their nationalities. We are communicating with relevant foreign embassies in China to keep them updated. As to the situation on the Nepalese side, nearly 100 Chinese nationals remain missing there. The Chinese Embassy in Nepal is seeking further verification with the Nepalese side and has put out a safety alert. Again we advise Chinese nationals there to move to safety and take precautions against secondary hazards. The Chinese Embassy in Nepal is available at all hours and will do its utmost to assist Chinese nationals in need. NHK: We have learned that a group of Japanese lawmakers visiting China met today with an official of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee. Could you provide more details about the meeting? Does the foreign ministry have any comment on it? Lin Jian: Chinese competent authorities will release information on the meeting in due course. The root cause of the serious difficulties in bilateral relations lies in the erroneous remarks and actions on Taiwan and in the fields of military and security made by those running the Japanese government. They should heed and value the voice of reason in Japan, do serious soul-searching, correct the wrongdoings, abide by the four political documents, and safeguard the political foundation of China-Japan relations with concrete actions. AFP: The U.S. law enforcement on Tuesday announced the seizure of Internet domains, allegedly used by Chinese hackers to target government agencies and critical infrastructure. The Justice Department and FBI said the seized domains were used by a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group, known as “QTFY” and by hacking platforms, known as “QScan” and “QTRouter.” I wonder if the foreign ministry can comment on this? Lin Jian: We notice relevant reports. China firmly opposes hacking and combats it in accordance with the law. China also firmly opposes spreading disinformation for political agenda. The so-called “statement” lacks evidence and confuses right and wrong. China strongly deplores and firmly opposes the U.S.’s wrong practice of slinging mud at China under the pretext of cybersecurity. The U.S. has been widely condemned as the world’s largest “hacking empire” and “eavesdropping empire,” with a blemished record and solid evidence to prove it. China has grave concerns with the U.S. on cybersecurity. The cases previously exposed, including the National Security Agency attacking and pre-positioning capability to disrupt China’s National Time Service Center, have laid bare the U.S. administration’s dangerous practice of carrying out cyberattacks on China’s critical infrastructure and pre-positioning cyberattack capabilities for potential large-scale destructive operations in the future. The U.S. side, however, has never made a response on this issue. When it comes to cyber issues, China and the U.S. are countries with big influence. The two sides should take the lead to safeguard and follow the international rules on cyberspace and jointly build a relationship in cyberspace featured by peace, stability and mutual respect. We urge the U.S. to quit double standards and political manipulation, take a responsible and constructive approach, and properly handle the risks on cybersecurity by equal-footed dialogue and consultation with China. Bloomberg: We’re wondering, with relation to the flash floods in Nepal and landslides in Tibet, could you give a breakdown of the nationalities of the foreign nationals? We’re also wondering if China is planning to take any special action to deal with the crisis? The second question is on Chinese leader’s planned trip to the U.S. We’re wondering if the Chinese leader will go to the U.S., and what conditions need to be met to ensure the trip is happening? Lin Jian: On your first question, affected by the disaster, the specific information is still under verification. The rescue efforts at the site are being carried out intensively and in an orderly manner. On your second question, China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state this year. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump declared a national emergency on Wednesday over foreign-made equipment inside the country’s electric grid, saying that the growing need for power has made the system a target for hostile governments. Can China provide a comment on this? Lin Jian: China consistently opposes overstretching the concept of national security to go after foreign enterprises. It is hoped that the U.S. will provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment for companies of all countries. Reuters: About the mudslide in Gyirong County. We know that China is still verifying a lot of information about the foreigners, but is there any profile of the foreigners that we can have information about? Are they tourists? Are they workers who are working on projects along the border? Lin Jian: According to the initial information we have, there are tourists and pilgrims among those unaccounted for. For more specifics, as I just mentioned, we are waiting for further verification, which is still ongoing due to conditions on the ground.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 26, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
CCTV: China announced that President Xi Jinping will attend the 2026 SCO Summit. What message does China hope to convey? Lin Jian: This year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO. Over the past 25 years, member states have upheld the Shanghai Spirit, worked in solidarity and coordination, and deepened all-round cooperation. The SCO has grown into a comprehensive regional cooperation organization that covers the biggest area and population with enormous development potential, successfully explored a new type of regional cooperation, and set an example of a new type of international relations. Last year’s SCO Summit in Tianjin provided strategic planning on the development of the SCO for the next decade, and opened up a new stage of high-quality development of the organization. At this year’s summit in Bishkek, President Xi Jinping will have in-depth exchanges of views with participating leaders on deepening SCO cooperation in various fields under the new circumstances and major international and regional issues of our times. They will provide guidance for the SCO’s high-quality development and participation in the reform and development of the global governance system. China stands ready to work with various parties to build up consensus and write a new chapter of cooperation in Bishkek, and contribute to security, stability, development and revitalization of regional countries and the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. CGTN: President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Could you share with us the arrangement? What’s China’s expectation on growing its ties with the two countries? Lin Jian: China and Kyrgyzstan are good neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, good friends of mutual trust, and good partners with a common pursuit. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations 34 years ago, the two countries have been treating each other with good faith and sincerity, setting a stellar example of mutual support and mutual success among neighboring countries. In recent years, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have grown by leaps and bounds, with consolidating political mutual trust, fruitful outcomes in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, numerous highlights of people-to-people exchanges, and close and effective coordination on international occasions. Last year, President Xi Jinping had three meetings with President Japarov, steering China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation into a golden period of rapid development. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in key areas, and international and regional situation with President Japarov in their talks, and attend various state events. China looks forward to working with Kyrgyzstan to take this visit as an opportunity to promote high-quality development of mutually beneficial cooperation on all fronts, add new dimensions to the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, and bring more benefits to the two peoples. Egypt is the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President El-Sisi, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful outcomes in cooperation across various fields, and engaged in increasingly frequent people-to-people exchanges and close and effective coordination on multilateral occasions. China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has grown by leaps and bounds, and been at its best in history, setting a stellar example of solidarity, collaboration and mutual benefit among developing countries. This visit marks President Xi Jinping’s first state visit to Egypt in 10 years. As we are celebrating the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Egypt diplomatic relations, this visit carries great significance in building on the past achievements and charting the future. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with President El-Sisi. They will have an in-depth exchange of views on China-Egypt relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest. Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other’s modernization, so that we can jointly draw a new chapter of China-Egypt relations and make positive contributions to peace and stability in the region and beyond. Bloomberg: Following Scott Bessent’s public comments on the so-called “Economic D-Day” regarding sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, has there been any communication between the U.S. and the Chinese side on this matter? And if so, can you provide any additional details? Lin Jian: I have no information to share at the moment. Bloomberg: Chinese authorities are urging Chinese citizens in Eswatini to evacuate, and urging others not to visit the country, citing local security and scamming concerns. Can you elaborate a little bit on some of the thinking behind this advisory? Could you also tell me how many Chinese citizens roughly live in Eswatini? Lin Jian: Eswatini is faced with a complex security situation with rampant telecom fraud and online gambling and extremely high safety risks. Issuing travel advisories is a common practice worldwide. Committed to a people-centered approach and diplomacy for the people, we will do everything necessary to safeguard the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese citizens overseas. Bloomberg: Would you be able to give me some examples of other similar travel advisories that China has issued, specifically regarding scamming and related risks? And also, China doesn’t have diplomatic relations with Eswatini. Is that a factor in this advisory or is it unrelated? Lin Jian: We have issued similar advisories. For this one, I need to stress that given the extremely high safety risks and rampant telecom fraud and online gambling in Eswatini, the Chinese government, for the safety of Chinese nationals, issued the travel advisory after prudent evaluation. Bloomberg: Going back a little bit to the SCO and also the trips to Egypt by President Xi Jinping. You mentioned that international and regional issues would be on the agendas in both Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Specifically, can I ask you, how prominent do you think Iran will feature in the discussions? Is there anything a bit more specific you could share about what regional conflicts in particular will be dealt with as part of this trip? Lin Jian: For more about the visits, we will release readouts in due course. Please stay tuned. Bloomberg: We know that Canada has matched the tariffs that President Trump set, including 50 percent on items such as dairy and steel. Broadly speaking, is there some kind of opinion or perspective that you could share from the Chinese foreign ministry’s point of view in terms of the actions that Canada or perhaps other countries might take in response to Trump’s tariff war. Is there some advice, for example, or some comments that you can provide? Lin Jian: China believes that economic and trade concerns should be addressed through dialogue and consultation on an equal footing.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Japanese Politicians Paying Respects to the Yasukuni War Shrine Which Honors Class-A War Criminals
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-15
Q: August 15 marks the day of Japan’s unconditional surrender in the Second World War. Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni war shrine today, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine. What’s your comment? A: China strongly deplores Japan’s negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan. During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes. The Yasukuni war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism. It is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression. No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians’ true intention which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan’s war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization. This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. To view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan’s ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions.
